question: Does the installed SGLang build support session-aware radix caching, and what does the observation-masking result actually license for a cache-adjusted cost comparison on our stack?

budget.stop_reason: each required question answered by a primary source (vendor page + arXiv abstract) or moved to open_questions; the remaining questions are about our own build and rows, which are measurements, not research

sources.version_scope: current-main, unversioned; NOT pinned to the build at :8012 (0.0.0.dev1+g4ccff141d)
sources.claim_taken: Session-aware radix caching is enabled with --enable-session-radix-cache, is implemented only by UnifiedRadixCache, protects KV by session reference rather than pinning, requires the application to pass the same top-level session_id on every request, and releases references via POST /close_session; eviction drains unreferenced nodes before referenced ones, then follows the configured policy; component cascade is full -> SWA -> mamba.

In SWE-agent on SWE-bench Verified across five model configurations, a simple environment observation-masking strategy halves cost relative to the raw agent while matching, and sometimes slightly exceeding, the solve rate of LLM summarization; a hybrid approach reduces cost a further 7% (vs masking) and 11% (vs summarization); initial evidence generalises to the OpenHands scaffold.

claims.claim: SGLang's session-aware radix cache protects KV by session reference (soft, evictable) and changes eviction ORDER only; it does not pin memory and does not change what the model sees.
claims.evidence: 'Session references are soft protection, not memory pins. Referenced KV can still be evicted when reclaiming unreferenced KV is insufficient.'

claims.claim: The /close_session endpoint is required for correct lifecycle; closing dereferences but does not immediately free KV.
claims.evidence: 'Closing removes the session's references but does not immediately free its KV. The KV remains reusable and returns to the normal eviction order.'

claims.claim: Session accounting tracks each UnifiedRadixCache component separately, with cascade rules full -> SWA -> mamba.
claims.evidence: 'Evicting an internal Full node also evicts its SWA and Mamba data; evicting SWA also evicts Mamba data; evicting Mamba affects only Mamba.'

claims.claim: The feature is compiled into the build serving :8012 (modules, flag, endpoint and request field all present).

The feature is OFF on the production configuration (enable_session_radix_cache=false), so no observation in this pilot can be attributed to it; enabling it would be a different engine fingerprint and would need a restart.
claims.evidence: Local check L5: enable_session_radix_cache=false in /get_server_info of the running server.

claims.claim: Whether the OpenAI-compatible chat/completions path actually honours session_id end-to-end on this build is NOT established; presence of the field in the protocol models is necessary, not sufficient.
claims.evidence: L4 shows the field exists; no request with session_id was sent, and the feature is disabled, so behaviour is untested.

claims.claim: At the pilot's context sizes (roughly 5-40K prompt tokens against a 1.58M-token pool) the session cache cannot be exercised discriminatingly: it only changes eviction order under memory pressure, and the STATE-CLIFF sweep showed residency under pressure is only bracketed at >=128 documents wide.
claims.evidence: C1 (order-only effect under pressure) plus experiments/context-cache/cells/STATE-CLIFF/RESIDENCY-BOUNDS.md (bracket width 128-136 docs).

claims.claim: Observation masking halves agent cost while matching summarization's solve rate on SWE-bench Verified with SWE-agent, and a hybrid masking+summarization variant saves a further 7% (vs masking) / 11% (vs summarization).
claims.evidence: Abstract, verbatim: 'a simple environment observation masking strategy halves cost relative to the raw agent while matching, and sometimes slightly exceeding, the solve rate of LLM summarization' and 'further reduces costs by 7% and 11% compared to just observation masking or LLM summarization, respectively'.

claims.claim: The paper's cost axis is provider-priced tokens for a hosted setup; it does not report engine-side cache reuse or uncached prefill, so its result does not transfer to a cache-adjusted comparison without local measurement.
claims.evidence: The abstract reports cost and solve rate only; no KV/prefix-cache accounting, no engine fingerprint, and the models are not occamy-1.0.

claims.claim: Observation masking is a prefix REWRITE (older observations are omitted), so on a prefix-caching engine the treatment can increase uncached prefill even while shrinking the payload -- the exact conflation handoff/DO_NOT_REDO.md §1 forbids.
claims.evidence: Masking removes earlier observation text from the prompt; DO_NOT_REDO §1 records payload -24.2% / billed -2.4% on a comparable change.

changes_plan: Session-aware radix cache is recorded as AVAILABLE-BUT-OFF: a separate fingerprinted experiment requiring a restart, with no discriminating test at pilot pressure. It is not a candidate for this pilot and must not be credited with any measured difference.

Arm C (masking + one checkpoint) is justified by s2 only as a quality-neutral hypothesis; the gate still requires it to win on cache-adjusted cost per verified success measured on our rows, because C10 says the paper's cost axis can invert here.
open_questions: Does the OpenAI chat/completions route honour session_id on 0.0.0.dev1+g4ccff141d? Requires a variant container with --enable-session-radix-cache; not attempted (would be a new engine fingerprint).
What is the marginal prefill cost per uncached token on this box? Measured in E1/E2 (latency and uncached-token counts), not researchable.
Is there a trustworthy GPU price schedule for this host? None in the workspace; the gate therefore uses uncached-input + output tokens as a labelled proxy, never dollars.
